newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up on lack of dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up on lack of dollar demand.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Tuesday stronger against the dollar at 35.88/89 against the day's opening 35.93/95 on lack of demand, dealers said.
They said movement in the exchange rate was one-way with the rupee appreciating steadily on lack of dollar demand.
"There was a good deal of corporate selling today," said a dealer. "There was hardly any demand for dollars."
"Dollar selling was initially cautious as some players still expected a large state-run bank to hit the market. But as no demand emerged, corporates stepped up dollar sales and the rupee moved up."
He said the rupee traded at a high of 35.885 and a low of 35.935 on Tuesday.
Dealers said forward premia fell on receiving pressure as exporters sold forward dollars. They said prospects of easing domestic liquidity also aided sentiment.
The Reserve Bank of India effects a 50 basis point cut in banks' cash reserve ratio (CRR) to 10.5 percent on Saturday.
The premia on six-month dollars fell to an annualised 6.86 percent against Monday's close of 7.18 percent.
